book: Haug, Computer-Aided Kinematics and Dynamics of Mechanical Systems, Vol. I (1989)
section: 12.6 Dynamic Analysis of a Governor Mechanism
extraction: Tables read twice: once from the PDF page images, once from 220 dpi crops of the same pages. Every value below matched on both reads. Figures digitized from 300 dpi renders by a pixel scan of the plot column at each time; axis calibration from the tick marks.
units: SI. Global y is vertical (up); gravity acts along -y.

gravity.note: Inferred: the steady state of Section 12.6.2 gives 11.0175 rad/s with g = 9.8 and 11.0212 rad/s with g = 9.80665 (book 11.0174).

joints.format: Body-fixed points (x', y', z'). The joint axis of a body is Q - P.

REV1.note: Q_j - P_j = (0, -1, 0) is antiparallel to Q_i - P_i; a revolute joint needs only parallel axes.

steady_state.note: Ball 1 e3 is printed +0.3827. REV2 puts the hinge at x' = -0.16 of ball 1, and the hinge is at the spindle origin (0, 0.2, 0); this needs e3 = -0.3827. With e3 = +0.3827 the hinge would be at (0, -0.0263, 0). The builder uses -0.3827.

external_torque.T_e: 0 for t <= 1 s, linear to -25 N m at t = 2 s, -25 N m after (about +y, opposing the spin)
external_torque.T_s: C * dl, dl = spring deformation = downward collar movement from the steady state
external_torque.solver_support: No force element with a state-dependent torque. examples/haug/governor.py applies T_e + T_s as a constant body torque per coupling step and rebuilds the system each step (Heun predictor-corrector on dl). The coupling error at dt = 0.02 s is below 4e-6 (checked against dt = 0.0025 s).

dynamic_analysis.start: steady state of Table 12.6.6, omega = 11.0174 rad/s
dynamic_analysis.figure_units: The collar y axes of Figs. 12.6.3 and 12.6.5 are labeled (m) but read 4.6 to 5.1 for a collar at y = 0.05 m; the plotted unit is 0.01 m. The values below are in the plotted unit.
dynamic_analysis.read_method: Raw pixel readings. 'anchor' is the reading of the initial plateau, where the exact value is known (collar 5.000, omega 11.0174); a test subtracts the anchor offset.

fig_12_6_3.identification_note: At t = 3 s the 4.9019 run is the dash-dot (k = 2000) curve; the dotted curve lies near 4.93 there and the scan column hits a gap between its dots.

fig_12_6_5.note: C = 17,500 grows into an oscillation after t = 6 s (unstable feedback, p. 488); later points depend on the oscillation phase and are not tabulated.

dynamic_analysis.read_uncertainty: 1 percent of the plotted axis span (Fig. 12.6.3: 0.004, Fig. 12.6.4: 0.02, Fig. 12.6.5: 0.005, Fig. 12.6.6: 0.01), plus the ripple half amplitude where the book curve ripples, because the ripple phase of an independent integration need not match point by point
consistency_notes: Figs. 12.6.4 (k = 1000) and 12.6.6 (C = 12,500) show the same nominal case; at t = 8 s they read 10.595 and 10.577 rad/s.
The exact final steady state of the book model for k = 1000, C = 12,500 is omega = 10.5818 rad/s, collar y = 4.800 (torque balance 12500 * dl = 25 N m).

The k = 2000 and k = 3000 curves of Figs. 12.6.3-12.6.4 are close to solver runs with k = 3000 and k = 5000: at t = 5 s the book k = 2000 curve reads collar 4.844, omega 10.154; the solver with k = 3000 gives 4.843, 10.144.
